meta.title: Ahd — Your covenant with the Qur'an
meta.description: Plan your hifz, commit to it, practice it, and never lose it. Ahd turns one decision into a daily plan of new memorization, recent revision and old revision — with a deadline that can only ever move closer.

hero.lead: Ahd turns one decision — the whole Qur'an in two years, or three, or five — into a plan for every single day. New memorization, recent revision, and old revision, scheduled for you. And a deadline that can only ever move closer.

hadith.arabic: تَعَاهَدُوا هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ، فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ لَهُوَ أَشَدُّ تَفَلُّتًا مِنَ الْإِبِلِ فِي عُقُلِهَا
hadith.translation: Keep renewing your covenant with the Qur'an. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it slips away faster than camels from their tethers.
hadith.note: ‘Ahd — عَهْد — means covenant. That hadith is the whole reason this app exists.

problem.title: Hifz rarely fails at memorizing. It fails at keeping.

endless.title: The plan that never ends
endless.body: You begin with a goal and no date. Every missed day quietly becomes tomorrow. Three years later the goal has not moved a single page.

forget.title: Memorize a lot, forget more
forget.body: New pages feel like progress. Meanwhile the pages from six months ago are dissolving, and nothing anywhere tells you.

blind.title: No idea what is weak
blind.body: You find out mid-salah, standing in front of people, exactly which page you no longer have.

alone.title: Alone by week three
alone.body: Motivation is not a plan. Without a teacher, a circle, or something holding you to it, hifz quietly stops.

covenant.title: A deadline that only moves closer.
covenant.lead: When you create a plan you choose an end date. From that moment the date is one-directional. You may pull it earlier. You may never push it back — not once, not by a single day.
covenant.refusedBody: A covenant you can move is not a covenant. Fall behind and the workload redistributes across the days you have left — the time itself never grows.
covenant.acceptedBody: Your covenant just became more ambitious, and today's portion grew with it. This direction is always open to you.

db.title: Enforced in the database
db.body: Not a disabled button. A check constraint and a trigger in Postgres. There is no path through the app that can extend your deadline.

log.title: Written to a permanent log
log.body: Every amendment is appended to an immutable history you can read. Nothing about your plan is ever silently rewritten.

rukhsah.title: Rukhsah days, for real life
rukhsah.body: Illness and travel happen. A rukhsah day protects your streak and lifts today's obligation — and still does not move the date. You fix the budget at the start and can never top it up.

tracks.title: Three obligations. Every single day.
tracks.lead: This is how hifz has been taught for centuries. Ahd generates all three tracks for you each morning, from your plan and from what your memory actually looks like today.

sabaq.name: Sabaq
sabaq.body: Today's new portion — your plan's daily dose, measured down to the line, not a vague page.

sabqi.name: Sabqi
sabqi.body: The last seven days of new memorization, recited again every day while it is still fragile enough to lose.

manzil.name: Manzil
manzil.body: Everything older, on a rotating cycle — with your weakest pages pulled to the front automatically, instead of a blind rotation.

tracks.footnote: All three green, or the day does not count.

mosaic.title: Every page you hold. And every page you are losing.
mosaic.body: All 604 pages of the mushaf, coloured by strength. Strength rises when you recite cleanly and decays on its own when you do not — because a page you have not touched in forty days is not the page you memorized. One glance and you know the entire state of your hifz.

practice.title: Six ways to actually test yourself.
practice.lead: Reading a page again is not revision. Producing it from memory is. Every mistake you make is recorded at word level and comes back to find you.

hide.title: Progressive hide
hide.body: The text fades word by word, then line by line, until the page is blank and only you are left.

firstWord.title: First-word prompt
firstWord.body: Only the opening word of each ayah remains. The rest is yours to produce.

next.title: What comes next?
next.body: Hear or see an ayah, then recite the one that follows. The single most useful drill there is.

shuffle.title: Ayah shuffle
shuffle.body: The ayahs of a page arrive scrambled. Put the page back in order.

gap.title: Fill the gap
gap.body: Random words are lifted out of the page. Restore them exactly.

mutashabihat.title: Mutashabihat duel
mutashabihat.body: Two nearly identical passages, side by side. Which is which? The hardest part of hifz, finally drilled directly.

everything.title: Built for how you really study.

offline.title: Works with no signal
offline.body: Read, drill and mark progress on the bus, in the masjid, on a journey. It syncs when you are back.

audio.title: Audio built for hifz
audio.body: A–B loop with a repeat count, word-level highlighting synced to the recitation, and adjustable speed without the pitch shifting.
audio.reciters: Mishary Alafasy · Alijon Qori · Badr al-Turki · Al-Husary · Al-Minshawi

record.title: Record yourself
record.body: Recite into your phone, listen back against the reciter, and keep every recording attached to that page's history.

halaqah.title: Halaqah circles
halaqah.body: A private circle with an invite code. Your friends, your teacher, a shared board — and accountability that encourages rather than shames.

teacher.title: A real teacher, if you have one
teacher.body: Submit a recitation. Your teacher marks pass or repeat, pins the exact ayahs you stumbled on, and sends a voice note back.

reminders.title: Reminders that mean it
reminders.body: A nudge at the time you said you would study, and a second, quieter one if the day is still empty by evening.

languages.title: Uzbek, English, Russian
languages.body: The full interface in all three from day one, with translations beside the Arabic. Arabic interface with right-to-left layout is next.

yours.title: Your data is yours
yours.body: Export everything as JSON or CSV whenever you like, and delete your account for real — not hidden, not deactivated, gone.

cta.title: Make your covenant today.
cta.body: Choose the whole Qur'an in two years, or a single juz in three months. Write your intention in your own words. Then let the plan hold you to it.

footer.textNotice: Qur'anic text is verified against the King Fahd Complex mushaf. Every translation shows its translator and licence.
footer.rights: Built as an act of service. May Allah accept it.

about.title: Why Ahd exists
about.lead: Most hifz does not fail at memorizing. It fails at keeping.

sections.heading: One hadith, and a whole product
body: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said: “Keep renewing your covenant with the Qur’an. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it slips away faster than camels from their tethers.”
That is the whole design brief. Not “learn faster” — hold on. Ahd (عهد) means covenant, and the app is named for the thing the hadith asks of us.

sections.heading: A deadline that only moves closer
body: Almost every plan quietly fails the same way: a goal with no date, and every missed day silently becoming tomorrow. Three years later the goal has not moved a page.

So in Ahd the date is one-directional. You may pull it closer. You may never push it back — not once, not by a day. That rule is not a disabled button; it is a constraint and a trigger inside the database, so no path through the app can extend a deadline.
Fall behind and the work redistributes across the days you have left. The plan tightens on you rather than relaxing.

sections.heading: Rukhsah, because life happens
body: Illness and travel are real. A rukhsah day protects your streak and lifts that day’s obligation — and still does not move your deadline. You fix the budget when you sign and can never top it up.
Without that, one bout of flu ends the whole thing. With it, the rule can stay absolute.

sections.heading: Revision is not optional
body: Every day gives you three obligations, the way hifz has been taught for centuries: sabaq, the new portion; sabqi, the last seven days while they are still fragile; and manzil, everything older, on a cycle that pulls your weakest pages to the front.
Strength decays on its own. A page you have not touched in forty days is not the page you memorized, and the app says so instead of pretending otherwise.

sections.heading: About the text
body: The Arabic is the Uthmani script, checked on every build against facts about the mushaf that are not negotiable — 114 surahs, 6236 ayahs, 604 populated pages — and against landmarks anyone can verify in a physical copy. A checksum guards it afterwards, so corruption is loud rather than silent.
Every translation names its translator. No Qur’anic text, translation or tafsir here is generated by a machine, and none ever will be.

sections.heading: Who made it, and what it costs
body: Ahd is built in Uzbekistan, in Uzbek, English and Russian. It costs nothing, carries no advertising, and has nothing to sell you. Your data is yours: exportable whenever you want, and deletable for real.
It is offered as an act of service. May Allah accept it.

faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: The things people actually ask before they commit.

items.q: Can I extend my deadline if I fall behind?
items.a: No. That is the one thing Ahd will never do, and the reason it works. You can pull the date closer, and the daily portion recalculates across the days you have left. If the pace becomes genuinely unsustainable you can reduce your scope once — thirty juz down to fifteen, say — keeping the same date. Scope may shrink; time may never grow.

items.q: What happens if I get ill or travel?
items.a: Use a rukhsah day. It protects your streak and removes that day’s obligation without moving your deadline. You choose the budget when you make your covenant — twelve days a year by default — and it cannot be topped up afterwards.

items.q: Do I need an account to read the Qur’an?
items.a: No. The whole mushaf is readable with translation at /quran, with no sign-up, and you can mark pages read on your device. An account is only needed for anything that has to follow you between devices: your covenant, your progress and your revision schedule.
Muhammad Sodik Muhammad Yusuf for Uzbek, Elmir Kuliev for Russian, and Saheeh International for English. Each is named on the page it appears on.
عهد — a covenant, a binding promise. It comes from the hadith about renewing your covenant with the Qur’an before it slips away.

items.q: How long should I give myself?
items.a: The whole Qur’an is 604 pages, or 9,060 lines. Three years works out at about nine lines a day; two years at thirteen. Choose the pace you can still keep on a bad week, not the one that sounds impressive today.
Not yet. The site works properly on a phone and can be installed to your home screen. Android and iOS apps come later, built from the same codebase.

items.q: I found a mistake in the text.
items.a: Please tell us immediately — that is the most important message you could send. Use the contact page and we will correct it and say what changed.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Written by reading the database schema, not by copying a template.

sections.heading: What is stored
body: Your email address. A hash of your password — Argon2id, never the password itself. Your display name, language, theme, timezone, chosen reciter and the time you said you study.
Your covenant: its scope, dates, rest days and rukhsah budget, plus an immutable log of every amendment to it. Your progress: which pages you have memorized and how strong each one is.

Your sessions, so you can see where you are signed in and end them: a hash of each session token, plus the browser and IP that created it. Sign-in events, so we can lock an account that is being guessed at.

sections.heading: What is not stored
body: No advertising identifiers. No third-party tracking scripts. Nothing is sold or shared with anyone, because there is nobody to sell it to and no plan to have one.
Reading the Qur’an without an account stores nothing on our side at all. Pages you mark read live in your own browser.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: In a PostgreSQL database hosted by Neon in Frankfurt, Germany, and served by Vercel from the same city. Verification codes are sent by email through Gmail.

sections.heading: Getting it back, or getting rid of it
body: You can export everything as JSON or CSV. You can delete your account, and deletion means deletion — the rows are removed, not flagged as hidden, and everything attached to them goes with them.

sections.heading: Email
body: We send verification codes, password resets, and — if you turn them on — daily reminders and weekly summaries. Nothing else. There is no newsletter and no marketing.

sections.heading: Children
body: Ahd is for anyone memorizing the Qur’an, including children studying with a teacher or parent. We ask for no more than the account needs.

terms.title: Terms
terms.lead: Short, because there is not much to agree to.

sections.heading: What Ahd is
body: A free tool for planning and keeping Qur’an memorization. It is not a teacher, and it does not replace one. Nothing here is a religious ruling.

sections.heading: The covenant rule
body: When you make a covenant you are choosing a constraint on purpose. The deadline can only move closer, and this is enforced in the database rather than in the interface. Please do not ask us to extend one — we cannot, and the refusal is the point.
If a plan becomes genuinely impossible you may reduce its scope once, or abandon it and begin again. An abandoned plan stays in your history with how far you got, honestly.

sections.heading: Your account
body: Keep your password to yourself. You are responsible for what happens under your account. Tell us if you think someone else has got into it and we will help you end every session.

sections.heading: The Qur’anic text
body: The Arabic and the translations come from their respective sources and remain theirs. They are provided for reading and study. If you find an error, report it — we treat that as urgent.

sections.heading: No warranty
body: Ahd is provided as it is. We work hard to keep it correct and available, but we cannot promise it will never be wrong or never be down. Do not rely on it as your only record of your hifz.

sections.heading: Changes
body: If these terms change in a way that matters, you will be told in the app rather than quietly. Continuing to use Ahd afterwards means you accept the change.
